title: Screening and informed consent

draft.title: Screening and informed consent
card: a check done before a person starts activity or testing. It looks for health risks, such as a heart condition, an injury or a medical condition that exercise could make worse.
the person understands what the testing involves, including its purpose and possible risks, and freely agrees to take part.

Screening is done first, so the results can guide whether it is safe to test and how to adjust the test. A person who is asked to sign a form without it being explained has not given informed consent.
Consent can be withdrawn. A person can stop at any time. For a young person, a parent or guardian usually also needs to agree.
draft.remember: Screening finds the risks before testing. Informed consent means the person understands and agrees.

a.q: Why is a health screening questionnaire completed before a fitness test?
opts: To find health risks that the test could make worse
To measure the person's fitness level before the test
To give the person a score to compare with others
To teach the person how to do each test correctly
a.why: Screening looks for risks, such as a heart condition, so the tester can decide if testing is safe. Measuring fitness is the job of the test itself, not the screening.
a.clue: Think about what must be known before the test begins.

b.q: Before a fitness test, Sam's coach hands him a form and says, "Just sign here." He signs without reading it. Why has Sam not given informed consent?
opts: He did not understand what the testing involves
He did not complete a health screening form
He did not pay to take part in the testing
He did not tell the coach about his past injuries
b.why: Informed consent needs the person to understand the purpose and risks of the testing and then agree. A signature alone does not show this. Screening is a separate step, so skipping it does not decide whether consent was informed.
b.clue: A signature is not the same as understanding.

a.best: To find health risks that the test could make worse

b.best: He did not understand what the testing involves
